source.document: FCA Service Bulletin 31-002-19 — Scan Tool Support Before and After Collision Repair (September 25, 2019). Additional reference: Chrysler Group LLC Collision Bulletin 31-003-12 — Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) Module Sensor and Bracket Guidelines During Collision Repair and Damage Estimating (March 30, 2012).
source.file: makes/sources/stellantis/ (Chrysler scan position statement, ACC bulletin 31-003-12)
source.note: Bulletin 31-003-12 predates the Stellantis formation — it was published by Chrysler Group LLC and most directly applies to legacy Chrysler/Jeep/Dodge/Ram vehicles. Fiat and Alfa Romeo use separate European-sourced service info. Per-component calibration triggers for newer Stellantis vehicles must be obtained from FCA Service Information (TechAuthority).

general_requirements: Per FCA Bulletin 31-002-19: Safety and security related systems (ABS, SRS, ORC, active head restraints, forward facing camera and radar, blind spot monitoring, and other automated ADAS) must be tested for fault codes before and after collision repair.

post_collision_universal_triggers.trigger_lead: Per FCA, any of the following conditions could trigger DTCs prior to or during collision repairs, requiring pre- and post-repair scan:
triggers: Vehicle is involved in an accident or collision, even though the damage may appear minor
Vehicles have been in an accident with or without airbag deployment
Voltage loss, including battery disconnects and Hybrid battery disabling
Significant vehicle disassembly including, but not limited to, bumpers, door handles, headlamps, and mirrors

components.component: Driver Assist Sensor Module (DASM) - Forward Windshield Camera
triggers: DASM and/or DASM bracket have been removed
A new windshield is being installed to the vehicle
Calibration Not Learned DTC (C008F-00) is present
Sensor Adjustment Required DTC (C14A4-00) is present

components.location: Front of vehicle, in the ACC sensor mounting bracket
components.calibration_note: Per Chrysler Bulletin 31-003-12: the three plastic ball socket clips in the sensor mounting bracket must be replaced each time the ACC sensor is removed from and reinstalled onto the mounting bracket. The adjustable ball studs, ACC sensor, and ACC sensor bracket cannot be repaired — if ineffective or damaged the sensor assembly must be replaced. 2007-2010 Chrysler 300 models use a different alignment procedure with Miller special tools 9965 and 9649.
triggers: ACC sensor or sensor-and-bracket assembly is removed and reinstalled or replaced
Front end structural repairs are performed
Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) indicates ACC sensor adjustment is required

components.calibration_note: Multistage airbags with multiple initiators (squibs) must be checked to determine that all squibs were used during the deployment event. Typically all initiators are exhausted during deployment, but it is possible for only one to have been exhausted.
triggers: Any airbag deployment event has occurred
Prior to removing deployed airbags from the vehicle for disposal

notes_for_other_components: Per shop practice confirmed against available FCA/Stellantis service info: Stellantis vehicles do not have a published blind spot calibration, post-collision occupant/zero-point calibration, surround view calibration, or parking sensor calibration. The only calibrations documented are the DASM forward camera and the ACC front radar. If newer Stellantis platforms introduce additional procedures they would need to be sourced from FCA Service Information (techauthority.com).
